\section[despedir]{despedir — to fire, to dismiss; (despedir-se) to say goodbye}

\label{lesson:PT-C356-despedir}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the candidate, then the Portuguese for to hire.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: despedir}
\textbf{despedir} — \textquotedblleft{}to fire, to dismiss; (despedir-se) to say goodbye\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
A fábrica despediu cinquenta trabalhadores.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{The factory fired fifty workers.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Despedir-se de alguém} — to say goodbye to someone. Conjugated \emph{despeço, despedes, despede}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{despedir} is formed from Latin \emph{dē} and \emph{expetere} \textquotedblleft{}to seek after, to ask for\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB, Lewis \& Short), built on \emph{petere} \textquotedblleft{}to seek\textquotedblright{}; it first meant \textquotedblleft{}to ask leave to go\textquotedblright{}, and then \textquotedblleft{}to send away\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

  \item \emph{Say it:} a sentence of your own with \emph{despedir}

\section[a demissão]{a demissão — the resignation}

\label{lesson:PT-C356-demissao}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to hire, then the Portuguese for to fire.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: a demissão}
\textbf{a demissão} — \textquotedblleft{}the resignation\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Ela apresentou a demissão ao chefe.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{She handed in her resignation to the boss.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Apresentar a demissão} — to hand in your notice. In Brazil, \emph{demissão} is also being fired.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{demissão} is a learned borrowing from Latin \emph{dīmissiō} \textquotedblleft{}a sending out, a sending away\textquotedblright{} (Lewis \& Short), from \emph{dīmittere} \textquotedblleft{}to send away\textquotedblright{}, built on \emph{mittere} \textquotedblleft{}to send\textquotedblright{}.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[o despedimento]{o despedimento — the dismissal, the sacking}

\label{lesson:PT-C356-despedimento}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for to fire, then the Portuguese for the resignation.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o despedimento}
\textbf{o despedimento} — \textquotedblleft{}the dismissal, the sacking\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
Houve muitos despedimentos este ano na fábrica.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{There were many dismissals at the factory this year.}
\end{quote}

European Portuguese; in Brazil \emph{a demissão}. \emph{Despedimento coletivo} — collective dismissal.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{despedimento} is built on \emph{despedir} \textquotedblleft{}to dismiss\textquotedblright{} with \emph{-mento}; the verb is formed from Latin \emph{dē} and \emph{expetere} \textquotedblleft{}to seek after\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB, Lewis \& Short).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
\end{grammarlens}

\section[desempregado]{desempregado — unemployed, out of work}

\label{lesson:PT-C356-desempregado}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the resignation, then the Portuguese for the dismissal.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: desempregado}
\textbf{desempregado} — \textquotedblleft{}unemployed, out of work\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O meu primo está desempregado há seis meses.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{My cousin has been out of work for six months.}
\end{quote}

Also a noun: \emph{os desempregados}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{desempregado} is built from \emph{des-} \textquotedblleft{}not\textquotedblright{} and \emph{empregado} \textquotedblleft{}employed\textquotedblright{}, the participle of \emph{empregar}, which is inherited from Latin \emph{implicāre} \textquotedblleft{}to fold into, to involve\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.

\section[o desemprego]{o desemprego — the unemployment}

\label{lesson:PT-C356-desemprego}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Portuguese for the dismissal, then the Portuguese for unemployed.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: o desemprego}
\textbf{o desemprego} — \textquotedblleft{}the unemployment\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
O desemprego subiu no inverno.
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{Unemployment rose in the winter.}
\end{quote}

\emph{Estar no desemprego} — to be out of work.

\begin{cousinweb}
\emph{desemprego} is built from \emph{des-} and \emph{emprego} \textquotedblleft{}job\textquotedblright{}, on \emph{empregar}, which is inherited from Latin \emph{implicāre} \textquotedblleft{}to fold into, to involve\textquotedblright{} (EtymDB).
\end{cousinweb}

One more word for telling, explaining and describing at B1.
